Omar Rivera: Prepare benchmark harness & sample prompts (due 2026-03-13)

summary: AE + SE from Redwood ran a POC scoping call with Argent Bank (CTO, Head of ML, DevOps) focusing on workload characterization: expected QPS/concurrency, token distribution, latency targets, and benchmark plan. Customer wants a 4-week POC to validate cost and latency with priority on fraud detection inference and chat assistance. Key constraints: peak bursts to 120 QPS, average 18 QPS, 6 concurrent long-context sessions, P95 latency target <= 350ms for short responses. Next steps: pricing proposal, benchmark spreadsheet, infra deep-dive for private sandbox.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Omar's our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Lena Park: Good thanks. Quick note, we have Diego from product on as well.
[00:13] Omar Rivera: Great, quick agenda: align on success criteria, surface workload numbers (QPS, concurrency, token distributions), and agree a benchmark plan.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Sounds good. We're primarily scoping a POC for our fraud scoring + chat support assistant. We want to validate latency and unit cost.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Perfect. To start, can you share current traffic patterns? average and peak QPS?
[00:36] Samir Patel: Sure, averaged over last month: baseline ~18 QPS, typical working hours spike to 45 QPS, but we have event-driven bursts up to ~120 QPS for a few minutes.
[00:48] Ruth Gomez: Those bursts are during settlement windows; short lived but sharp.
[00:53] Omar Rivera: Helpful. When you say bursts to 120, is that sustained for >5 mins or more like 1-2 minute spikes?
[00:59] Samir Patel: Usually 1-3 minutes, rarely longer. 95% of traffic is under 60 QPS.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Good to know. For concurrency, how many simultaneous sessions do you expect holding long contexts?
[01:11] Samir Patel: For the chat assistant maybe 4-6 long-lived sessions per region (they keep context). Fraud scoring is stateless but high QPS.
[01:19] Diego Alvarez: For fraud calls, the payloads are small JSONs, typically 80-200 tokens in, and 20-40 tokens out. For chat, inputs vary widely—average 400 tokens in, 350 out.
[01:33] Omar Rivera: So two main workload profiles: short stateless scoring (80-200 in / 20-40 out) and long-context chat (avg 400/350). Any heavy multimodal or embeddings work?
[01:45] Samir Patel: We'll run embeddings in a later phase; not in this POC. Focus on generation and scoring.
[01:50] Maya Chen: And what are your latency SLOs? P95 or P99 targets?
[01:54] Samir Patel: For fraud scoring, P95 <= 200ms would be ideal but we can accept up to 350ms. For chat, P95 <= 800ms is OK; P99 less critical.
[02:05] Ruth Gomez: Also security: we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), and option for a private VPC or on-prem for production. POC can run in a private sandbox VPC.
[02:15] Maya Chen: We support that. We'll share our security / compliance pack. For the POC scope, are you looking for hosted or dedicated capacity?
[02:22] Lena Park: We want to evaluate hosted first; if numbers look good we'll move to dedicated. But we need to emulate private network conditions.
[02:29] Omar Rivera: Makes sense. For benchmarking, we'll want representative sample payloads and a target QPS curve: steady-state ~20 QPS, diurnal spikes to 45, and a burst test to 120 QPS for 2 minutes. Any constraints on sequence lengths?
[02:41] Samir Patel: Max sequence length for chat sessions is 8k tokens. But most are shorter; the average we said was 400. Fraud payloads are <512 tokens.
[02:50] Omar Rivera: Great. We'll design the runner to vary payload sizes and simulate KV cache hits for chat to reflect long-context sessions. Note: auto transcription often writes K V cash or K V cache weirdly, but we mean KV cache.
[03:03] Diego Alvarez: Also, some calls require model determinism—consistency across runs. We want to compare Redwood's recommended model variants and quantization settings.
[03:11] Maya Chen: We'll propose two model paths: a latency-optimized variant (quantized, lower context overhead) and a quality-optimized variant. We'll run A/B benchmarks and measure cost per 1M tokens and P95 latency.
[03:23] Samir Patel: For success criteria: <=350ms P95 for scoring at target QPS, and cost under $X per 1M tokens — I'll get budget guardrails. Also accuracy/regression thresholds for chat outputs (we'll supply eval prompts).
[03:36] Omar Rivera: Good. Can you share your evaluation prompts and a small golden set so we can run qualitative checks?
[03:41] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll scrub PII and provide ~200 examples across both workloads.
[03:46] Maya Chen: Timeline—we typically do a 3-4 week POC: week 0 (onboarding, dataset ingest, infra setup), week 1 (baseline benchmarks), week 2 (A/B and tuning), week 3 (final reporting). Is that workable?
[03:58] Lena Park: 4 weeks works for us. We want an internal review at end of week 2.
[04:03] Omar Rivera: Noted. For the POC infra we'll need: sample dataset, target QPS curve, VPC peering info for sandbox, list of allowed egress IPs, and an SRE contact for runbooks.
[04:15] Ruth Gomez: I'll provide the VPC peering + firewall details; note that we require outbound S3 access for logs.
[04:21] Maya Chen: On measurement, we'll record token-level cost, latency percentiles, error rates, and trace IDs to map requests. We'll supply a benchmark spreadsheet template.
[04:31] Samir Patel: Do you do continuous batching / caching automatically or do we need to configure?
[04:35] Omar Rivera: Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and prefix/KV caching automatically; you can tune batch window and cache TTL. We'll surface recommendations based on your token distribution.
[04:45] Diego Alvarez: For the quantization path — any risk to inference quality? We need to see quality delta metrics.
[04:50] Omar Rivera: We'll run the quantized model side-by-side and compute BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and manual evals on the golden set to quantify delta.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Regarding cost projection, we'll run a model that shows unit cost by QPS and token mix, plus a sensitivity analysis for burst patterns. We'll include dedicated pricing options if you want reserved capacity.
[05:10] Lena Park: Good. Can you also include failure modes and fallback policies? In production we need graceful degradation to a cheaper model or queueing.
[05:18] Omar Rivera: Absolutely. We'll show routing policies: prefer low-latency pool, fallback to cheaper variant or region, and queue/backpressure options.
[05:26] Samir Patel: What about observability? We need token-level cost, traces per request, per-model dashboards, and rollback triggers.
[05:33] Maya Chen: Redwood Console covers token cost breakdown, per-route latency, tracing hooks, and an alerting integration. We'll demo those in the mid-POC check-in.
[05:41] Ruth Gomez: For PII, we'll scrub the sample dataset, but does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[05:46] Maya Chen: Yes, KMS/HSM options for private deployments. For the hosted POC we can enable encryption-at-rest and limited retention; for production we can move to customer-managed keys.
[05:55] Diego Alvarez: In terms of success metrics we also want to run a 2-minute sustained 120 QPS soak to validate autoscaling and latency.
[06:03] Omar Rivera: We'll include that in the benchmark plan, plus a ramp test. We'll log resource utilization and tail latencies.
[06:11] Maya Chen: Any legal or procurement blockers we should be aware of?
[06:15] Lena Park: Standard review; procurement will need the SOC 2 report and a draft contract. We can start the procurement loop in parallel.
[06:23] Maya Chen: Great. Next steps recap: Maya to send POC proposal & pricing (due 3/12), Omar to share benchmark harness and spreadsheet (due 3/13), Ruth to share VPC details (due 3/16), Samir to send logs and golden set (due 3/13). Schedule infra deep-dive for 3/17.
[06:40] Diego Alvarez: Quick question — for concurrency of long contexts, is KV cache preserved across sessions if we pin sessions?
[06:46] Omar Rivera: Yes, KV cache persists per session; we can also show different cache TTLs to measure tradeoffs.
[06:53] Samir Patel: Awesome. If we get results that look good, we'd like to move to a dedicated reserved pool for production.
[06:59] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include reserved capacity estimates in the proposal.
[07:04] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[07:08] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and proposal.
[07:12] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript has occasional ASR errors, some product names mis-transcribed (e.g., K V cache). References to attachments: "benchmark spreadsheet" (Redwood link to be shared), "security pack" (Redwood security docs).
